title: Rain on the roof
scene: a quiet room under a wooden roof while steady rain falls, at any time of day
scene_conditions: Time of day is not fixed and may be any time; avoid light, sky or time-of-day assumptions.
voice: Calm, warm, unhurried voice; close and conversational, never theatrical.

closing_rest.music: Keep the same quiet bed with the rain through the rest, fading it over the final 15 seconds so the last line is spoken over rain alone.

music.prompt: Instrumental only. An almost still ambient bed for a guided meditation: warm analog synth pads and soft bowed strings holding long tones in D major, around 60 BPM with no discernible pulse. Slow attacks, long releases, very few note changes, gentle tape saturation, a large soft plate reverb. Calm and steady from start to finish, with no percussion, no lead melody and no builds.
music.mix_notes: Keep the bed well below the voice with the rain still recognizable. Soften the presence range so it never competes with a quiet voice, smooth any musical swells, and duck slowly across whole spoken passages rather than word by word.
music.gain_reference: 1.0 is the calibrated quiet music bed

cues.direction: Bring the bed in slowly under the rain and voice; the opening belongs to the rain.
Let the same texture recede during the breathing rest.
Withdraw the music before the short invitation in 06 so its rest is rain only.
Return with the same bed, no new theme announcing it.
Fade out over the last 15 seconds of the closing rest; the final line is spoken over rain.

ambience.prompt: Steady light rain on a wooden roof, heard from inside a quiet room. Even, continuous patter with soft drips from the eaves.
ambience.mix_notes: The rain is the primary anchor: present from the first second, recognizable under the voice, still there after the last word.

one_shots.prompt: A single soft singing bowl strike in a quiet room, warm tone with a long natural decay.
one_shots.direction: Opening bell; the first words arrive as it decays.
Closing bell after the final line, a little softer.

phrases.text: [exhales] Let's start where you are, with the rain on the roof and a place to rest.
The rain doesn't keep time. Some drops land close and sharp; others blur into a soft hiss further off.
Listen to the whole of it for a while, without picking anything out.
Now the body. There's weight here, meeting whatever holds it: a chair, a cushion, the floor.
Let that support do some of the work.
Leave its pace alone. Feel where it moves most easily, the belly perhaps, or the chest.
Thoughts come and go the way the rain does, heavier for a while, then lighter.
When you notice you've drifted into planning or remembering, that's fine. It's still there to come back to.
Still here. Rain on the roof. Breath coming and going.
If your attention wandered, it hasn't gone anywhere wrong. It can come back from wherever it went.
The rain will keep going without you.
